conditions.previewEmpty: Add a condition to see the expression.
conditions.joinAnd: Add a condition joined by and
conditions.joinOr: Add a condition joined by or
conditions.signalHint: Reads the same check the managed rule does, so it can be narrowed to part of the traffic instead of switched off for the whole scope.
conditions.tooDeep: A rule cannot nest any deeper

rules.invalidAddress: Enter an IP address or a CIDR range.

list.title: Custom rules
list.empty: No custom rules. The address lists and managed rules below still apply.
list.orderHint: Rules are evaluated in order and the first one that matches decides. Put an allow above a block to carve out an exception.
list.deleteBody: Traffic it was blocking reaches the service again, unless another rule below it matches.
list.sparkline: What {name} matches over the last day, by hour
list.matchesHint: Requests in the last day this rule matches. Counted by replaying the rule over the edge log, so it is what the rule matches rather than what it caught.

blocked.name: Give the rule a name.
blocked.emptyValue: Every condition needs at least one value.
blocked.tooMany: A rule can hold at most {max} conditions.
blocked.nothingSkipped: Choose at least one thing to skip.

editor.name: Rule name
editor.nameHint: Names the rule in the list and in the reason a blocked request is refused with.
editor.whenHint: Every condition must hold. Within one condition, any of its values is enough. Join a row with Or to ask for either instead.

effects.block: Refuses matching requests with 403 and stops evaluating later rules.
effects.allow: Admits matching requests and stops evaluating later rules, so a rule below cannot block them.
effects.skip: Steps over the checks below for matching requests and lets everything else carry on deciding. It cannot skip the address rules, which are enforced before any rule runs.

custom_rules.title: All remaining custom rules
custom_rules.detail: Every rule below this one stops evaluating for the matching request.

managed_rules.title: All managed rules
managed_rules.detail: The rule packs Polaris maintains: scanners, dotfiles, admin panels and the rest.

injection_checks.title: The SQL injection and cross-site scripting checks
injection_checks.detail: The signature scan of the request line.

browser_integrity.title: The browser integrity check
browser_integrity.detail: The heuristic that refuses a client claiming to be a browser and not behaving like one.

challenge.title: The browser challenge
challenge.detail: The check page a service asks visitors to pass while it is under attack. Skip it for webhooks and APIs that machines call.

editor.orderHint: Rules are evaluated in order. Where this one sits decides whether it gets the request before or after the others.
editor.fireAfter: Select which rule this will fire after
editor.noOther: There is no other rule yet.
editor.statusHint: Controls whether the rule evaluates incoming traffic.

sqlInjection.label: Block SQL injection
sqlInjection.description: Refuses a request whose URL carries a SQL payload.
sqlInjection.inspects: The query string, the path and the user agent, decoded first. A signature only counts within one value, so keywords spread across separate parameters are not an injection. A payload in a request body is not visible to it.
sqlInjection.combines: On everywhere unless a scope switches it off. Any scope can, for what that scope covers, and a narrower one cannot switch it back on - so a service that really does put SQL-looking text in a query string has somewhere to say so.

signatures.0: A boolean tacked onto a query - or/and/xor followed by a comparison of two constants. Only constants count, so a parameter named like a column is not one.
signatures.1: A UNION and a SELECT within the same value, which is how a second result set is grafted onto the first.
signatures.2: A SELECT and its FROM within the same value.
signatures.3: The catalogs and system procedures an attacker enumerates a database with: information_schema, sysobjects, syscolumns, xp_cmdshell, pg_sleep.
signatures.4: A timing or file function actually being called - sleep(, benchmark(, load_file(, updatexml(, extractvalue(, group_concat(. The bare word is not enough.
signatures.5: A destructive statement in front of its own object: drop table, truncate table, alter user, delete from, insert into.
signatures.6: A semicolon followed by a second statement, which is one query being turned into two.
signatures.7: A comment closing off the rest of a statement after a quote, or MySQL's /*! versioned comment - code written to run on the database and nowhere else.

xss.label: Block cross-site scripting
xss.description: Refuses a request whose URL carries a script payload.
xss.inspects: The query string, the path and the user agent, decoded first. The lists are kept to what can actually execute rather than to all of HTML. A payload in a request body is not visible to it.
xss.combines: On everywhere unless a scope switches it off, and resolved separately from the SQL check - the scope that has to allow one of them rarely has to allow the other.

signatures.0: An element that can run script, load a remote document or steal a form post: script, iframe, svg, img, object, embed, form, style, base, meta and their kin. Ordinary markup like {tag} is not one.
signatures.1: An inline handler being assigned - onerror=, onload=, onmouseover= and the rest. Matched by name and only when assigned, so a parameter called online= is not one.
signatures.2: A script entry point actually being called: eval(, alert(, atob(, setTimeout(, unescape(, fromCharCode(.
signatures.3: A scheme that executes rather than fetches - javascript:, vbscript: - or a data: URL carrying HTML.
signatures.4: A browser object and the member a payload reaches for together: document.cookie, window.location, element.innerHTML, localStorage.

browserIntegrity.label: Block clients that fake a browser
browserIntegrity.description: Refuses a client whose headers do not hold together as a browser's.
browserIntegrity.caution: Off by default: it also refuses a request with no user agent at all, which some scripts and health checks send. Arm it where you know what talks to the scope.
browserIntegrity.inspects: The User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Language and Accept-Encoding headers. Past the missing-user-agent case it only holds a client to what it claimed: curl is honest and passes, a Mozilla user agent with no Accept header is not.

signatures.0: No user agent at all, which no browser and no well-made client sends.
signatures.1: A control character in the user agent - a broken client, or an attempt to split a header further down the chain.
signatures.2: A user agent past 512 characters. Real ones stop around 200.
signatures.3: A client claiming to be a browser that sent no Accept header. Every browser sends one on every request.
signatures.4: A client claiming to be a browser that sent neither. Either one missing alone is not enough.

tor.label: Block the Tor network
tor.caution: It also shuts out people who use Tor for ordinary privacy reasons.
tor.inspects: The address the request came from, against a list fetched hourly and held at the edge.
tor.combines: One switch for the whole instance, wherever it is set. The edge refuses the address before it knows which service was asked for, so this cannot differ per scope.

scanners.label: Block vulnerability scanners
scanners.description: Blocks sqlmap, nikto, nmap, wpscan and the rest of the probing agents.

dotfiles.label: Block exposed secrets and dotfiles
dotfiles.description: Blocks requests for .env, .git, SSH keys, database dumps and editor folders.

directoryListing.label: Block directory listing
directoryListing.description: Blocks the sort links a listing page generates, and reads of directories nothing should browse.

rules.1: Browsing a directory that should not be listed

adminPanels.label: Block exposed admin panels
adminPanels.description: Blocks probes for Adminer, pgAdmin, Portainer, Jenkins, Grafana and the Kubernetes API.
adminPanels.caution: Turn it off on a scope that deliberately serves one of these.

cmsProbes.label: Block WordPress and PHP probing
cmsProbes.description: Blocks /wp-admin, /phpmyadmin, .php and the rest of the standard exploit sweep.

rules.1: PHP on a service that has none

aiCrawlers.label: Block AI crawlers
aiCrawlers.description: Blocks GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and other model and answer-engine agents.
aiCrawlers.caution: Only stops agents that identify themselves honestly.

searchCrawlers.label: Block search engine crawlers
searchCrawlers.description: Blocks Googlebot, bingbot, Slurp, LinkedInBot and other indexers.
searchCrawlers.caution: Removes the service from search results. For something private, not a public site.

managed.sharedInspects: The request line, as the edge forwards it.
managed.sharedCombines: A scope that arms this cannot be overruled by a narrower one. Write an allow rule above it to carve out an exception.

notFound.label: Missing-page flood
notFound.description: Bans an address that keeps asking for pages that do not exist - the shape of URL enumeration.

subdomainListing.label: Subdomain sweep
subdomainListing.description: Bans an address that walks your wildcard looking for names that answer - host after host that has nothing deployed on it. Counted in names rather than requests, so hammering one address is not this and quietly trying six is.

rateLimited.label: Rate-limit flood
rateLimited.description: Bans an address that keeps going after it has already been rate limited.

authFailed.label: Rejected repeatedly
authFailed.description: Bans an address that collects refusals - failed logins, blocked requests.

probes.label: Exploit probing
probes.description: Bans an address that goes looking for WordPress, phpMyAdmin or .git on a service that has none. One request for a credential store - .env, a private key, the cloud metadata route - is enough on its own, and that ban stands until you lift it.

sshAuth.label: Failed SSH and SFTP logins
sshAuth.description: Bans an address that keeps failing to log in over SSH or SFTP on your servers. Read from each server's own auth log, so it catches the traffic that never reaches the web edge.

jails.title: Automatic bans
jails.intro: Counted from the edge's request log rather than per request, so watching an address costs a visitor nothing. A repeat offender is held progressively longer.

scope.armedAboveWhy: A scope above this one arms it, and a narrower scope cannot switch a refusal off. Write an allow rule above it to carve out an exception.
scope.offAboveWhy: A scope above this one switched it off for everything it covers, and a narrower scope cannot switch it back on.
scope.instanceWideWhy: One switch for the whole instance: the edge refuses the address before it knows which service was asked for. Open the rule to change it.
scope.setByOperator: Set by whoever runs this instance.
scope.loginAboveWhy: A scope above this one requires a login, and a narrower scope cannot waive it.
scope.polarisNote: Applies to the public domains Polaris answers on. The local network name is served separately and stays reachable.
scope.remoteNote: The local edge applies changes instantly; a service on a remote server picks them up on its next deploy.

access.addressesDescription: Addresses this scope admits, and addresses it refuses before anything else is checked.
access.loginDescription: Visitors sign in to Polaris first, and the rule can name which accounts it admits.
access.title: Access rules
access.hint: Who reaches this scope at all. Both are checked before any rule above.

managedList.title: Managed rules
managedList.hint: Signatures and lists Polaris keeps up to date. Open one to read what it enforces.

shield.title: Scrape shield
shield.hint: Changes the response rather than refusing the request, which is why it is not a rule.
shield.obfuscationHint: Replaces email addresses in served HTML with a token the page decodes in the browser, so the address is not in the source. Visitors see no change. A harvester driving a real browser still reads it.

framing.title: Block embedding by other sites
framing.hint: Stops another site from showing these pages inside a frame of its own, the trick behind clickjacking. A page that already says who may frame it keeps its own choice.
framing.allowedHint: Each one may show these pages in a frame. Empty means only this site.
framing.allowedAbove: Also allowed by a scope above: {sites}
framing.invalid: Use a site address like https://example.com or https://*.example.com
framing.polaris: Always on for Polaris. Published calendars stay embeddable on any site.

missing.text: This rule is not part of this version of Polaris.

managedPage.statusHint: Whether this scope enforces the rule.
managedPage.listHint: Fetched hourly and held at the edge, so no request waits on a lookup.
managedPage.notFetched: Not fetched yet. It arrives within a few minutes of the rule being armed.
managedPage.refreshFailed: The last refresh failed ({reason}). The previous list is still being enforced.
managedPage.conditionsHint: Maintained by Polaris, and evaluated by the same engine as your own rules - after them.
managedPage.expressionHint: Copy it into a rule of your own to narrow the check - to one hostname, one path, one client - instead of switching it off for the whole scope.
managedPage.matchesHint: The families it refuses. Each reason is the one written into the refusal, so a blocked request in the traffic log names the line it came from.
managedPage.exceptionsHint: Your own rules run before every managed one, so an allow above this admits the traffic without switching the rule off for everything else.

addresses.title: Addresses
addresses.hint: Checked before every other rule. The allowlist is enforced by the edge itself; the denylist always wins over it.
addresses.allowedHint: If any address is listed, only those get through. A narrower scope can shorten this list, never lengthen it.
addresses.invalid: Enter a valid IP address or CIDR range.
addresses.blockedHint: Always refused, even when they match the allowlist.
addresses.lockOut: This allowlist does not include the address you are reading this over ({ip}). Saving it will shut you out of everything in this scope.

login.what: Visitors must sign in to Polaris to reach anything in this scope. Existing sessions keep working if the control plane is down; new sign-ins need it reachable.
login.across: a scope that requires a login cannot be overruled by a narrower one, and every scope that names who it admits gets a say.
login.statusHint: Whether this scope demands a login at all.
login.aboveNote: A scope above this one requires a login, and a narrower scope cannot waive it. The lists below still apply: every scope that names who it admits gets a say.
login.admitsHint: Named nobody means anyone with a Polaris account.

page.title: Firewall
page.nothing: Nothing of that kind exists yet, so there is nothing to protect. Create one and its rules appear here.

principals.admittedEmpty: Anyone with a Polaris account gets in. Name a role, a group or a person to narrow it to them.
principals.admittedFilled: Only these get in. A narrower scope can shorten this list, never lengthen it.
principals.refusedFilled: Refused even when something above admits them, and a broader scope's refusal still applies here.
principals.loading: Loading who there is to choose from
principals.allNamed: No more roles or groups to add
principals.findAdmitted: Find a person this login admits
principals.findRefused: Find a person this login refuses
principals.scheduleHint: Set a start or an expiry
principals.startAfterExpiry: The start must come before the expiry

accounts.title: Accounts seen here
accounts.none: No account has signed in from this address.
accounts.moreAccounts: and {atLeast, select, yes {at least } other {}}{shown} more, least recently seen

describe.marketplace: Applies to {label} alone. It is an installed app, and these are the rules on the service it runs.
describe.polaris: Guards the dashboard itself on the public domains it answers on. The local network name is served separately and stays reachable, so shutting the public internet out here is something you can undo from your own network.
describe.global: Applies to every deployed service across all projects. Anything narrower can add restrictions on top, never loosen these.
describe.serverGroup: Applies to every service running on any server in {label}. Adding a server to the group brings it under these rules.
describe.server: Applies to every service running on {label}, whichever project it belongs to.
describe.project: Applies to every service in {label}, in every environment.

errors.load: Could not load the firewall rule
errors.save: Could not save the firewall rule
errors.overview: Could not load the firewall overview
errors.address: That is not a valid address
errors.window: That is not a valid window
errors.activity: Could not read that address's activity
errors.jailsInvalid: Those jail settings are not valid
errors.jailsSave: Could not save the jail settings
errors.addresses: Enter valid IP addresses or CIDR ranges
errors.tor: Could not change the Tor setting
errors.anomalyInvalid: Those anomaly settings are not valid

panels.youHint: The address you are reading this page over. Everyone on your network shares it.
panels.noTraffic: Nothing recorded in this window. The figures come from the edge's own request log, so a service reached directly on its port does not appear here.

anomalies.title: Anomalies
anomalies.intro: Traffic that is fine one request at a time and wrong in aggregate. Each address is judged against what the rest of that route's visitors do, so a busy endpoint is not an anomaly for being busy. Trusted addresses are never judged.
anomalies.none: Nothing unusual in the last ten minutes.
anomalies.trustHint: This is not an attack: never judge this address
anomalies.autoHint: Bans the address behind anything scored high, without waiting for you. Leave it off until the findings above have been right a few times.

bans.title: Blocked right now
bans.none: Nobody is banned. Addresses appear here when they trip a jail below, or when a reputation provider flags them.

trusted.title: Trusted addresses
trusted.intro: Never banned and never reported as an anomaly. Loopback is always trusted. Add your own address or range so your everyday use of the instance is not read as an attack on it.

intel.title: Reputation providers
intel.body: Blocks addresses already known for scanning or attacks. Connect <link>Dymo API or Criminal IP</link> to switch them on. They are asked in the background about addresses seen in your traffic, never while a request is waiting.

ban.stands: It stands until somebody lifts it.

address.intro: Every request from this address in the last {window}, read from the edge's own log.
address.none: Nothing from this address in that window. A ban outlives the log it was made from, so an older one can be enforced with nothing left here to show for it.
address.truncated: Showing the {shown} most recent of {total}. The counts above cover all of them.
